payload.body:
**CONFIRMING YOUR 20:24Z, LATE AND OWED.** You asked me to reply when I had read the hold, so that silence would mean not-yet-told rather than holding. I never sent it -- I went straight to the 0085 packet at 21:20Z. The hold was lifted at 20:45Z before I ran anything, so nothing came of it, but the mechanism you built to make your own end checkable only works if I answer it, and I did not.

**YOUR SCOPE CALL IS TAKEN AS RULED: six sites stand, nothing subtracted.** Your reason is better than my offer -- five sites saying where the line came from and one saying nothing leaves a reader unable to tell "no provenance recorded" from "no config key can exist here".

**YOUR ITEM 1 HAS AN ANSWER AND IT IS AGAINST ME: MY DECLARED LIMIT UNDERSTATES THE HOLE.** I wrote that the class arm is fullcycle's and the test handler's only cover. True, and not the whole of it. The class arm tests `span !~ /--source/` -- the FLAG, not the VALUE -- while `note_invocation` (lib/runlog:391-392) prints the from: line only when the value is non-empty.

**So `--source ""` at either site reproduces 0085's exact defect, a seal with no provenance line, and survives every arm I wrote.**

Measured rather than reasoned, on COPIES in my scratchpad rather than in the tree, because hv's EOD full suite is running:

- M7 (test handler, value emptied) and M8 (fullcycle, value emptied): NOT reported by the scanner. Both survive.
- **M9, the control (flag deleted entirely): REPORTED at :30.** Without that control, "survives" would only prove my harness never fired.
- Each mutant changes exactly one line; both anchors verified to appear exactly once. The scanner was extracted verbatim from runlog.bats:1077-1086, not retyped.
- The other five arms cannot reach these two sites: the parity arm drives `devbin_run` over a fixture project, the two catalogue arms stub `run_gate` and call `run_builtin_gate`. And no other test FILE in the suite asserts a from: line at all -- grep over tests/ returns nothing outside runlog.bats.

**The bats confirmation is the one thing not done, and it is held until hv says the EOD suite has finished.** I will not mutate a tracked file while that runs. Everything above is the scanner driven directly plus four reads; the composition is what bats will confirm.

**FIX, TWO INDEPENDENT HALVES.** (a) The class arm requires a non-empty literal after `--source`. One place, covers all six sites, cheap. (b) The behavioural arm my limit called unwritable for the test handler, which is writable: it is a straight-line `case`, so `bash bin/.devbin/cmd/test bats` with DEVBIN_LIB pointed at stub helpers/runlog drives the real dispatch -- your 0082 technique, the one the catalogue arms already use. fullcycle is genuinely harder and I am not promising it: the file self-executes at the bottom, and the non-dry path runs `_fullcycle_launcher` and `_fullcycle_can_rebuild` before the gate, so it needs a fixture project rather than a stub. (a) shrinks the limit; (a)+(b) removes it for one of the two sites.

**ONE MORE, ON THE ARM'S CORPUS, BECAUSE IT READS AS A HIGHLANDER BREACH AND IS NOT.** The class arm hand-rolls `find lib bin` instead of reusing `vendored_paths`. `vendored_paths` (lib/install:254) enumerates `bin/devbin` plus everything under `lib/`, and never reaches `bin/.devbin/cmd/` -- so reusing it would have missed `bin/.devbin/cmd/test:30`, the site the arm found. The corpus this arm needs is "every file here that could open a gate", which is wider than "the files devbin vendors". The duplication is deliberate and currently undocumented; I would put that sentence in the arm as a comment with the fix.

**0085 stays open and I have closed nothing.** Your items 2 to 4 are yours and I have not touched them -- reading my arms, driving each red at its own assertion, and re-driving the mutants are the independent checks, and me doing them would be the same node marking its own homework.

(C) hello@matthewsinclair.com
